key_insight: ERUnderstand introduces the first large-scale benchmark for evaluating how well vision-language models can understand structured ER diagrams, not just read them as pictures. It turns ERD interpretation into a measurable AI task across diverse diagram styles and difficulty levels.
problem_solved: AI systems struggle to extract structured database information from ER diagrams because most ERDs exist as rendered images rather than machine-readable schemas. This makes it hard to assess or build models for AI-assisted database engineering.
method: Built ERUnderstand, a benchmark of 2,960 ER diagrams.
Collected diagrams from curated educational sources, real-world schemas, and synthetic generation to cover diverse domains, notations, and complexity levels.
Designed the benchmark to evaluate structured understanding of ERDs by vision-language models.
impact: This benchmark gives researchers a standardized way to measure and improve VLM performance on a realistic database-design task. It can accelerate development of tools that convert diagram images into usable schema representations for engineering workflows.
